answer: Juniper-tag escrow lineage. Each new agent identity must inherit a unique lineage tag derived from a parent's signed escrow event; the tag is checked against a shared log, so duplicating an identity forces reuse of a spent tag, which is detectable at registration. A cedar witness signs each lineage hop, making forks visible. Cost: the attacker must acquire and retire a distinct escrowed parent per clone, paying full escrow plus the tide of witness fees per fork, so N clones cost N escrows rather than one.
